text.p: German electronics giant Siemens AG said on Friday it was considering setting up a joint venture with Taiwan's Mosel Vitelic Inc to make advanced dynamic random access memory chips, or DRAMs, in Taiwan.
"Siemens is considering the venture with Mosel, but the deal is yet to be finalised," a Siemens Taiwan spokeswoman told Reuters.
She declined to confirm local media reports that the project could be worth US$1.5 billion or give further details.
Mosel vice-president William Chen confirmed that a likely venture with Siemens is under negotiation.
"We are close to reaching a final agreement with Siemens to set up a venture to produce 64-megabit or 256-megabit DRAMs in Taiwan," Chen told Reuters.
"But since we haven't finalised the deal, we cannot reveal any more details, including the size and investment proportion of the venture," he said.
Taiwan's Economic Daily News on Friday put the project's investment at US$1.5 billion but gave no source for the figure.
Mosel is one of the island's leading DRAM makers.
